boundary_rationale: The book's opening word is אֵיכָ֣ה (oshb:Lam.1.1, byte tier), the verse-initial cry that gives this stretch its aleph line and frames a third-person report of the ruined capital: “How the city sits solitary, that was full of people! She has become as a widow, who was great among the nations!” web:Lam.1.1. The same voice names the daughter-of-Zion formula at web:Lam.1.6 inside “All majesty has departed from the daughter of Zion.” web:Lam.1.6 (this verse also carries a ketiv/qere note per the inventory, not engaged by the present reading; the formula itself recurs seven further times book-wide, sweep: 8 verses book-wide), and keeps the same distance through the roads, gates and priests of web:Lam.1.4. The report closes on “She has no comforter.” web:Lam.1.9 immediately followed by the first-person plea “See, Yahweh, my affliction; for the enemy has magnified himself.” web:Lam.1.9, a brief intrusion of Zion's own voice inside an otherwise third-person span (a per-bytes deviation from a plain city_lament reading, disclosed rather than smoothed over). The same verse completes the contiguous refrain אֵ֥ין מְנַחֵ֖ם לָ֑הּ (oshb:Lam.1.9, byte tier; roughly "she is without a comforter"; sweep: 3 verses contiguous, byte tier), and refrains close units under the owner-ruled seam law: the boundary sits here rather than folding this verse forward with the interjection that follows it.

No second-person form and no first-person-singular form stands anywhere across these ten verses; the boundary sits here because the verse that follows is where the first person begins: עֵינַי֙, מֵעַ֔י, כְּבֵדִ֔י and the suffix inside בַּת עַמִּ֑י (oshb:Lam.2.11, byte tier) together carry four first-person-singular pronominal suffixes, opening the narrator's own report of grief — the tier-1 voice change that carries this stretch's own boundary, not the mark layer that runs beneath every verse of the poem alike.

boundary_rationale: Zion's own prayer closes the poem: “Look, Yahweh, and see to whom you have done thus!” web:Lam.2.20, opening on the same petition imperative רְאֵ֤ה יְהוָה֙ וְֽהַבִּ֔יטָה (oshb:Lam.2.20, byte tier) that already stood at oshb:Lam.1.11 (sweep: 2 verses, byte tier), then presses that plea through the horror of women eating their own children and priest and prophet slain in the sanctuary before turning to the day of slaughter itself: “You have called, as in the day of a solemn assembly, my terrors on every side.” web:Lam.2.22. The three-token form בְּי֥וֹם אַף יְהוָ֖ה (oshb:Lam.2.22, byte tier; roughly "in the day of the anger of Yahweh") stands in exactly 1 verse book-wide (sweep: 1 verse book-wide, this three-token form) and so closes the poem as a form attested once, not a repeating pattern; the shorter token it opens with, בְּי֥וֹם (oshb:Lam.2.22, byte tier), is itself byte-identical to the token that opens the same wrath phrase at the poem's own aleph line, בְּי֥וֹם אַפּֽוֹ (oshb:Lam.2.1, byte tier; sweep: 2 verses, byte tier), so the poem's last verse closes an inclusio with its own first verse. The chapter's own PE mark closes web:Lam.2.22.

At the front seam, the imperative שִׁפְכִ֤י כַמַּ֨יִם֙ לִבֵּ֔ךְ נֹ֖כַח פְּנֵ֣י אֲדֹנָ֑י (oshb:Lam.2.19, byte tier; "pour out your heart like water before the face of the Lord"; this verse also carries a ketiv/qere note per the inventory, not engaged here) stands one verse ahead of this span's own opening prayer, and the same title, אֲדֹנָ֖י (oshb:Lam.2.20, byte tier), stands again inside its report of the sanctuary, so the divine title straddles the seam on both sides. The 1cs speaker and 2ms addressee carried across this span are equally available to the poem's own narrator, whose 1cs already stands at web:Lam.2.11 with 1cs verbs addressing the city at web:Lam.2.13, so the forms alone do not separate the personified city's voice from the narrator's.
